_doc: AUTHORED contract overlay for kit parts (ADR-043). Merged over the GENERATED manifest assets/.../kit/firebase_set.json by KitRegistry. Authored, never generated: this is the CollisionTable precedent, where a naming heuristic once shipped barracks_bunker.glb as SOFT COVER because its name contained 'rack' - a bunker you could shoot through. Author the entry; do not name your way into a material.
_why_this_file_exists: A kit part cannot use the monolith's mechanism. Destruction there matches the MESH name against FSB_STRUCTURE_KINDS, which works because gen_firebase.py stamped instances named fb_bunker_fighting_i*. The standalone kit GLBs were exported in July as a REVIEW artefact and their visible meshes carried Blender workbench names. On 2026-09-09 tools/add_kit_colliders.py renamed them and cut a -colonly twin per solid mesh, so the two contracts now agree by construction - but IDENTITY still comes from this file, not from a name, and that is deliberate. A stamped part knows its own id.

_retired._why: TWO BUNKER TYPES ONLY - his ruling, 2026-09-09: 'we just need two types of bunkers'. The two that survive are fb_bunker_fighting (the rifle bunker, the line position) and fb_bunker_mg (the crew-served position the compound is built around). They are also the only two bunkers that have ever had a .glb and a collider. Everything named here is refused by KitRegistry.contract_gap() and dropped from placeable_ids(), so dropping a .glb into the kit folder cannot quietly put a retired part back on the palette. THIS LIST DOES NOT TOUCH THE MONOLITH: fsb_main_v3.glb still ships sleeping bunkers and FSB_STRUCTURE_KINDS still carries fb_sleeping_bunker_i, because removing that row would make every sleeping bunker in the demo's firebase indestructible.
_retired.fb_sleeping_bunker: RETIRED from the kit palette 2026-09-09 by the two-bunker ruling. It never had a .glb - it was a manifest row and nothing else - so nothing is lost but the advertisement. Sleeping quarters are fb_hootch's job.

_fields.destructible: Destructible.HP_FOR kind, or "" for a DELIBERATE ruling that this part is not a structure. Never absent - an absent entry fails the stamp loudly, which is the point.
_fields.structure_meshes: Exact visible mesh names that ARE the structure. Explicit, never a prefix guess: fb_bunker_mg.glb also contains m60.002 and m60_pintle, and a machine gun is not a bunker. At most ONE per part - one Destructible takes all of a part's colliders.
_fields.soft: true = soft_cover (round passes at 0.8x, concealment). false = hard_surface. Earth, sandbag and timber are hard, and that is deliberate.
_fields.crew: Roles this part BRINGS when it is stamped, as bare strings. Read by KitRegistry, resolved by SitePlanner.site_plan_garrison() into the same {pos, occupation, men} post shape fsb_garrison_plan() emits. Strings, never enums - a WW1 part must be able to declare a role without anyone editing site_planner.gd.
_fields.demands: What must be present in the SAME plan for this part's crew to turn up. A TOC with nobody supplying 'command' is a hut. An unmet demand drops that part's crew and is printed, never silently ignored.
_fields.supplies: What this part provides to other parts' demands, as bare strings.
_fields.note: Why, when the answer is not obvious.

fb_bunker_fighting.note: ONE OF THE TWO BUNKERS HE KEPT (his ruling 2026-09-09: 'we just need two types of bunkers'). The rifle bunker is the line position. Mesh renamed from the Blender workbench name WB_bunker_rifle on 2026-09-09; the collider fb_bunker_fighting_000-colonly already carried the right base, so the two contracts had been half a system since July.

fb_bunker_mg.note: THE SECOND OF THE TWO BUNKERS HE KEPT. m60.002 and m60_pintle are the gun on top of it, deliberately excluded from the structure AND from collision - destroying the bunker must not require destroying the weapon as a separate structure, and a trimesh body round the gun is a wall between the player and the handles. Mesh renamed from WB_bunker_m60 on 2026-09-09.

fb_FoxholeSandbags.note: Collision added 2026-09-09 - a trimesh twin, not a box, because the hole in the middle is the whole point of a foxhole and a box hull is a lid over it.

fb_sandbag_heavy.note: Mesh renamed from sandbag_heavy on 2026-09-09; collision added the same day. 2.28 x 1.08 x 1.17 m.

fb_gate_assembly.note: NOT DELIBERATE ANY MORE. The July review export was five loose meshes with no colliders and a Blender .001 - watchtower_1.001, which imports as watchtower_1_001. On 2026-09-09 add_kit_colliders.py renamed all five (fb_gate_tower / fb_gate_leaf_l|r / fb_gate_post_l|r) and gave each a -colonly twin. The structure is the TOWER and it takes the existing 'tower' kind at 180 hp - the KIT_PART_CONTRACT proposed a new 'gate_house' row, and a watchtower on a gate is a tower, so no second kind was invented. The leaves and posts have collision and are scenery. His rebuilt gate house replaces this whole part; the wire gap in KIT_PART_CONTRACT section 4 is still open.

fb_emplacement_m101.note: DELIBERATE, and it stays deliberate: it is the howitzer, its ammunition and its baked crew rigs, and a sapper does not blow down a gun. What it was NOT allowed to stay is passable. 24 -colonly twins were added 2026-09-09 over the gun, carriage, wheels, shield, trails and the eight fb_sandbag_parapet segments round the pit. 95 meshes were deliberately left passable: 32 skinned crew rigs (they are people), the MC_ props in their hands, and 20 loose m101_round_* / m101_shell_* which a man walks over, not into.
